content: 1. The Antiretroviral Pregnancy Registry Steering Committee published an international interim report covering data from January 1, 1989, to July 31, 2015, which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 2. Yeni P and colleagues conducted a study on virological and immunological outcomes three years after initiating antiretroviral therapy with regimens containing non-nucleoside reverse transcriptase inhibitors, protease inhibitors, or both. This open-label randomized trial, known as INITIO, was published in The Lancet in 2006 (Volume 368, Pages 287–298). 3. Shafer RW and colleagues compared four-drug regimens and sequential three-drug regimens as initial therapy for HIV-1 infection. Their findings were published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2003 (Volume 349, Pages 2304–2315). 4. Riddler SA and colleagues evaluated class-sparing regimens for the initial treatment of HIV-1 infection. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2008 (Volume 358, Pages 2095–2106). 5. Worm SW and colleagues investigated the risk of myocardial infarction in HIV-infected patients exposed to specific antiretroviral drugs from the three major drug classes. This study, part of the D:A:D (Data Collection on Adverse Events of Anti-HIV Drugs) study, was published in the Journal of Infectious Diseases in 2010 (Volume 201, Pages 318–330). 6. Lang S and colleagues conducted a case-control study nested within the French Hospital Database on HIV (ANRS cohort CO4) to assess the impact of individual antiretroviral drugs on the risk of myocardial infarction in HIV-infected patients. Their findings were published in the Archives of Internal Medicine in 2010 (Volume 170, Pages 1228–1238). 7. Ryom L and colleagues explored the association between cardiovascular disease and the use of contemporary protease inhibitors. This information was accessed on July 1, 2017. 8. Squires K and colleagues compared once-daily atazanavir with efavirenz, each combined with fixed-dose zidovudine and lamivudine, as initial therapy for HIV-infected patients. Their study was published in the Journal of Acquired Immune Deficiency Syndromes in 2004 (Volume 36, Page 1011). 9. The IATT, UNICEF, and WHO released a fact sheet on lopinavir and ritonavir (LPV/r) oral pellets, which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 10. Nachman S and colleagues studied the pharmacokinetics, safety, and 48-week efficacy of oral raltegravir in HIV-1-infected children aged 2 to 18 years. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2014 (Volume 58, Pages 413–422). 11. Fowler MG and colleagues examined the benefits and risks of antiretroviral therapy for perinatal HIV prevention. Their study was published in the New England Journal of Medicine in 2016 (Volume 375, Pages 1726–1737). 12. Three new agreements were announced with the potential to expand access to innovative HIV treatment in lowand middle-income countries. This information was accessed on July 1, 2017. 13. Ripin D and Prabhu VR conducted a cost-savings analysis of a candidate universal antiretroviral regimen. Their findings were published in Current Opinion in HIV and AIDS in July 2017 (Volume 12, Issue 4, Pages 403–407). 14. The Global Price Reporting Mechanism online database was accessed on July 1, 2017. 15. Phillips AN and colleagues analyzed the cost-effectiveness of policy options when pretreatment NNRTI drug resistance is high. This information was accessed on July 1, 2017. 16. Molina J-M and colleagues compared once-daily dolutegravir versus darunavir plus ritonavir for treatment-naive adults with HIV-1 infection. The 96-week results from the FLAMINGO study were published in The Lancet HIV in 2016 (Volume 2, Pages e127–e136). 17. Phillips AN and colleagues modeled the effectiveness and cost-effectiveness of potential responses to high levels of transmitted HIV drug resistance in antiretroviral drug-naive populations beginning treatment. Their study was published in The Lancet HIV in 2014 (Volume 1, Pages e85–e93). 18. Rowley CF and colleagues reported a sharp increase in rates of HIV-transmitted drug resistance at antenatal clinics in Botswana, highlighting the need for routine surveillance. Their findings were published in the Journal of Antimicrobial Chemotherapy in 2016 (Volume 71, Pages 1361–1366). 19. A report from the Brazilian Ministry of Health analyzed transmitted HIV-1 resistance to antiretroviral therapy in treatment-naive patients in Brazil. This report was published in 2014. 20. The eighth edition of the Guía de manejo antirretroviral de las personas con VIH was accessed on July 1, 2017. 21. Guidelines for the use of antiretroviral agents in HIV-1-infected adults and adolescents were published, including recommendations for public health responses to pretreatment HIV drug resistance. 22. Hirsch MS and colleagues provided recommendations for antiretroviral drug resistance testing in adult HIV-1 infection. Their 2008 guidelines were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases (Volume 47, Pages 266–285). 23. Günthard HF and colleagues published 2016 recommendations for antiretroviral drugs for the treatment and prevention of HIV infection in adults. These guidelines were published in JAMA in 2016 (Volume 316, Pages 191–210). 24. The European AIDS Clinical Society guidelines were updated in January 2017 and accessed on July 1, 2017. 25. Sax PE and colleagues conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis to determine whether resistance testing should be performed for treatment-naive HIV-infected patients. Their findings were published in Clinical Infectious Diseases in 2005 (Volume 41, Pages 1316–1323). 26. Luz PM and colleagues analyzed the survival benefits of antiretroviral therapy in Brazil using a model-based approach. Their study was published in the Journal of the International AIDS Society in 2016 (Volume 19, Article 20623). 27. Duarte HA and colleagues conducted a cost-effectiveness analysis of pre-ART HIV drug resistance testing in Kenya. Their findings were presented at the 2017 Conference on Retroviruses and Opportunistic Infections (CROI) in Seattle. 28. Bennett DE and colleagues provided recommendations for the surveillance of transmitted HIV drug resistance in countries scaling up antiretroviral treatment. Their study was published in Antiviral Therapy in 2008 (Volume 13, Supplement 2, Pages 25–36). 29. The 2015 update on HIV drug resistance surveillance guidance was accessed on July 1, 2017. 30. WHO published a concept note on the surveillance of HIV drug resistance in adults initiating antiretroviral therapy (pretreatment HIV drug resistance), which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 31. WHO released consolidated guidelines on person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance, which were accessed on July 1, 2017. 32. The Global Action Plan on HIV Drug Resistance (2017–2021) was accessed on July 1, 2017. 33. Public health actions to prevent HIV drug resistance and respond to suboptimal performance of quality-of-care indicators were outlined in Web Annex 3, accessed on July 1, 2017. 34. WHO published consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, providing recommendations for a public health approach in its second edition. 35. UNAIDS introduced a gender assessment tool aimed at creating a gender-transformative HIV response, which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 36. WHO outlined guiding principles on ethical issues in HIV surveillance, which were accessed on July 1, 2017. 37. The Human Rights Costing Tool (HRCT) was developed to estimate the costs of programs aimed at reducing stigma and discrimination and increasing access to justice. This tool was accessed on July 1, 2017. 38. The Innov8 approach for reviewing national health programs was accessed on July 1, 2017. 39. The Health Equity Assessment Toolkit (HEAT) online database was accessed on July 1, 2017. 40. WHO published a concept note on the surveillance of HIV drug resistance in children newly diagnosed with HIV through early infant diagnosis, which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 41. WHO released a 2015 update on HIV drug resistance surveillance guidance, which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 42. WHO published a concept note on the surveillance of HIV drug resistance in adults receiving ART, which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 43. WHO released consolidated guidelines on person-centered HIV patient monitoring and case surveillance, which were accessed on July 1, 2017. 44. WHO published the Global Action Plan on HIV Drug Resistance (2017–2021), which was accessed on July 1, 2017. 45. Public health actions to prevent HIV drug resistance and respond to suboptimal performance of quality-of-care indicators were outlined in Web Annex 3, accessed on July 1, 2017. 46. WHO published consolidated guidelines on the use of antiretroviral drugs for treating and preventing HIV infection, providing recommendations for a public health approach in its second edition.
